HOTLIGH ZF8313 vs OLIGHT ArkPro Ultra

Which EDC flashlight is worth your pocket space? The budget RGB king at $22 or the premium flat-carry at $130?

Two Flashlights, Two Philosophies

These two EDC flashlights couldn't be more different in approach. The HOTLIGH ZF8313 costs $22 and throws 2000 lumens with RGB and UV modes from a compact magnetic body. The OLIGHT ArkPro Ultra costs nearly six times as much with a flat profile that disappears in your pocket and 1700 lumens of premium build quality. One is a feature-packed bargain; the other is a buy-it-for-life tool. Which one wins depends entirely on what you need a light for.

Brightness & Performance

The HOTLIGH actually out-lumens the OLIGHT on paper — 2000 vs 1700 lumens. But raw lumens aren't the whole story. The HOTLIGH's beam is a traditional circular throw with a hot center, while the OLIGHT uses a custom optic that creates a wider, more even spill. In practice, the OLIGHT feels more usable for close-to-medium tasks (reading, working under a hood, walking) while the HOTLIGH has the edge for distance spotting.

Where the HOTLIGH pulls ahead is heat management at max output — it does get hot after extended use. The OLIGHT's aluminum body dissipates heat more effectively, so you can run it longer on high without discomfort.

Features: The HOTLIGH Advantage

The HOTLIGH ZF8313 has a clear feature advantage: RGB lighting modes (great for camping ambiance, preserving night vision, or just showing off) and UV light (useful for detecting pet stains, counterfeit bills, or curing UV resin). The OLIGHT offers none of this — it's a pure white-light tool with nothing fancy.

The magnetic base on the HOTLIGH lets it stand upright on any metal surface, effectively acting as a work light. The OLIGHT's magnetic tail lets it hang from a car hood or metal beam. Both are useful, just oriented differently.

Pocket Carry: The OLIGHT Advantage

This is the OLIGHT's killer feature. The ArkPro Ultra is flat — genuinely flat — and disappears in a front pocket next to your wallet. You won't feel it when sitting, driving, or wearing slim pants. The HOTLIGH is a traditional cylindrical flashlight; it's compact for what it is, but you'll always know it's there.

If you want a flashlight you can carry every single day without noticing, the OLIGHT wins hands down. If you want a light that stays in a glovebox, backpack, or emergency kit, the HOTLIGH's traditional form factor is perfectly fine.

Build & Longevity

The OLIGHT is built to a different standard. Aircraft-grade aluminum, premium anodizing, and a reputation for reliability that justifies the price. OLIGHT has been making serious flashlights for years, and the ArkPro Ultra feels like a tool you'll hand down. The HOTLIGH is good for $22 — better than most Amazon budget lights — but it doesn't compete on materials, fit, or finish.

The Verdict

🏆 Best Value: HOTLIGH ZF8313

Six times cheaper, more lumens, RGB + UV, magnetic base — the HOTLIGH is the smarter buy for 90% of people.

🥇 Best Premium: OLIGHT ArkPro Ultra

The buy-it-for-life flat carry that disappears in your pocket. If you carry a light daily and want the best, this is it.

Buy the HOTLIGH ZF8313 if:

  • You want the most features for your money
  • You need RGB or UV modes (camping, repair work, detection)
  • You want a magnetic work light that stands on its own
  • 2000 lumens of max output matters to you
  • This is a glovebox, backpack, or emergency-kit light — not a daily pocket carry

Buy the OLIGHT ArkPro Ultra if:

  • You carry a flashlight every day and want it to disappear in your pocket
  • Build quality and longevity matter more than upfront cost
  • You value OLIGHT's reputation and warranty
  • You prefer a wide, even beam over raw max lumens
  • You're okay spending $130 on a tool you'll use daily for years
